mainTopic: Which sisters a כהן becomes טמא for, and whether a convert girl under three may marry a כהן
overview: A כהן may become טמא to bury his unmarried sister, the בתולה of ויקרא 21:3. The amud opens by asking which sisters count. One view uses the word 'קרובה' to include a sister who was only betrothed and then divorced. The גמרא explains why that word does not also include a מוכת עץ. רבי יוסי holds the reverse and splits the words 'לא היתה לאיש' into two teachings. Next, רבי שמעון בן יוחאי rules that a convert girl under three years and a day may marry a כהן, proving it from the war with מדין. רב הונא and a ברייתא show that those פסוקים are about age, not actual experience. The גמרא then explains how the girls were checked: the ציץ for מדין, and a wine barrel for יבש גלעד, because the ציץ is never used to punish Jews. Finally, רבי יהושע בן לוי rules like רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, and the גמרא tests whether this ruling was heard directly or inferred. רב נחמן בר יצחק still orders a כהן who relied on it to divorce his wife. The amud ends as a new ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי begins, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי שמעון's rule about fitness for a High Priest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that a כהן becomes טמא for his divorced ארוסה sister, using רבי שמעון's rule that he only does so for a sister fit to marry a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי שמעון say: if she is fit for a כהן גדול, he becomes טמא for her. If she is not fit for a כהן גדול, he does not become טמא for her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the opinion it was just explaining: that a כהן may become טמא for a sister who was betrothed and then divorced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A divorced woman is forbidden to every כהן, and certainly to a כהן גדול, even if she was only betrothed. So under רבי שמעון's test she is 'not fit for a כהן גדול', and her brother should not become טמא for her. That clashes with the view that he may.

keyTerms.meaning: fit to marry a High Priest
he becomes ritually impure for her (to bury her)

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Shimon say:
If she is fit for a High Priest, he becomes impure for her;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין רְאוּיָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל — אֵין מִטַּמֵּא לָהּ.
phrases.english: if she is not fit for a High Priest, he does not become impure for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the previous explanation (before this section) that a כהן becomes טמא for his divorced ארוסה sister.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a כהן becomes טמא for his sister who was betrothed and divorced.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A divorcée is not fit for a כהן גדול, and רבי שמעון ties the permission to become טמא to that fitness.

steps.title: The word 'near' adds the divorced betrothed sister
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the divorced ארוסה is different, because the תורה adds her with the word 'הקרובה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the Merciful One (the תורה) added her with the word 'קרובה' (near).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: this sister is a special case that the פסוק adds through an extra word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's general test still stands. But the word 'הקרובה' in the פסוק adds a sister who is still close to her brother, even though she fails the כהן גדול test. This is an exception made by the פסוק, not a rejection of the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One (the תורה) added / included

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question: if 'קרובה' adds cases beyond the basic rule, which cases does it add?

phrases.english: It is different there,
because the Merciful One included her with 'near'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:3. Here 'דרבי' means 'that added', not the title 'רבי'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special inclusion from an extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every sister unfit for a כהן גדול is excluded.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'קרובה' adds the divorced ארוסה as an exception to רבי שמעון's general test.

steps.title: Then the word should also include an accidentally injured woman
steps.stepSummary: If 'קרובה' adds a sister unfit for a כהן גדול, it should also add a מוכת עץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a מוכת עץ (a woman whose hymen was torn by accident) should also be included!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer: the same logic should cover a מוכת עץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוכת עץ is also unfit for a כהן גדול, who must marry a full בתולה. If 'קרובה' can include one unfit sister, why not this one as well? Yet this view does not let the כהן become טמא for her.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman whose hymen was torn by accident (literally 'struck by wood')

phrases.english: If so,
a woman injured by wood should also be included!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 by stretching its logic.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'קרובה' to include only the divorced ארוסה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מוכת עץ is equally unfit for a כהן גדול, so the same inclusion should apply to her.

steps.title: The word adds only one case, not two
steps.stepSummary: 'קרובה' includes just one extra case.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'קרובה' adds one case and not two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'קרובה' is only enough to add a single case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One added word can only bring in one extra case. So the פסוק cannot include both the divorced ארוסה and the מוכת עץ. One of them must stay excluded.

phrases.english: [The word] 'near' includes
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Here again רבי means 'adds', not the title.

phrases.english: one and not two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the inclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'קרובה' includes every sister unfit for a כהן גדול.

steps.title: Why choose the divorced sister over the injured one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason there is to include the divorced ארוסה rather than the מוכת עץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see (to choose this way)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the one added case is the divorced ארוסה and not the מוכת עץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only one case is added, the choice needs a reason. Without one, we could just as easily include the מוכת עץ and exclude the divorcée.

keyTerms.meaning: and what did you see? (what reason do you have to choose this way?)

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: Meaning: why include the divorcée and leave out the מוכת עץ, and not the other way around?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the choice left open by the answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to include the divorced ארוסה rather than the מוכת עץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both are unfit for a כהן גדול, so picking one seems arbitrary.

steps.title: A physical change happened to one, not the other
steps.stepSummary: The מוכת עץ had something happen to her body. The divorced ארוסה did not, so she is the one included.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (the מוכת עץ) had a physical act done to her body. That one (the divorced ארוסה) had no physical act done to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for the choice: physical change to the body versus none.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The divorced ארוסה is still physically a בתולה; only her legal status changed. The מוכת עץ actually lost her physical virginity. So the divorcée is closer to being a בתולה, and 'קרובה' includes her.

keyTerms.meaning: an act was done to her (a physical change to her body)

steps.whatToRemember: In this view, 'קרובה' adds only one case: the divorced ארוסה, who is still physically a בתולה. The מוכת עץ stays excluded because her body was changed.

phrases.english: This one — an act was done to her body;
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the מוכת עץ.

phrases.english: that one — no act was done to her body.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the divorced ארוסה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between the cases by a logical difference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The choice between the two cases is arbitrary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Physical change to the body excludes the מוכת עץ, so 'קרובה' includes the divorced ארוסה.

steps.title: Where does רבי יוסי get his view on the injured woman?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יוסי parted from רבי שמעון, he must agree with רבי מאיר about the מוכת עץ. The גמרא asks for his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי: since he left his partner (רבי שמעון), we learn that about a מוכת עץ he holds like רבי מאיר. Where does he learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new point: what רבי יוסי holds about the מוכת עץ, and what his source is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי appears with רבי שמעון on one ruling but is not listed with him on another. From this the גמרא infers that he agrees with רבי מאיר that a כהן does become טמא for a מוכת עץ, and it asks which words in the פסוק teach that.

keyTerms.meaning: he left his partner (did not join him in that ruling)
it follows that / we can infer
from where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei,
since he left his partner,
phrases.notes: His partner is רבי שמעון, who rules alone in the ברייתא on one of the cases.

phrases.english: it follows that regarding a woman injured by wood
he holds like Rabbi Meir,
from where does he learn it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the view discussed in steps 1-6 to רבי יוסי's opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the פסוק for רבי יוסי's view that a כהן becomes טמא for a מוכת עץ.

steps.title: From the words 'who has not been with a man'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns it from 'אשר לא היתה לאיש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From 'who has not been with a man'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוסי's source: the end of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק defines the sister as one who 'has not been with a man'. A מוכת עץ was never with a man, so she still counts, and her brother may become טמא for her.

keyTerms.meaning: has not been with a man (ויקרא 21:3)

phrases.english: From 'who has not been with a man'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לא היתה לאיש': only a woman who was with a man is excluded, so a מוכת עץ is included.

steps.title: But those words were already used for something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'לא היתה לאיש' was already used to exclude the divorced ארוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you already took it out (for a different law)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer: these same words were already used to teach a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that a כהן does not become טמא for his divorced ארוסה sister, and he learns that from 'לא היתה לאיש': she must not even have been betrothed. One phrase normally cannot teach two separate laws.

keyTerms.meaning: you already took it out (used it for another teaching)

phrases.english: But you already used it!
phrases.notes: It was used to teach that a sister who was betrothed and divorced is excluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'לא היתה לאיש' as the source for including the מוכת עץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase is already being used to exclude the divorced ארוסה, so it is not available to teach another law.

steps.title: The phrase is split into two teachings
steps.stepSummary: One law comes from 'לא היתה' and the other from 'לאיש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: One law is learned from 'has not been', and one law from 'with a man'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by dividing the phrase into two parts, each teaching its own law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא היתה' (she has not been, in any way) teaches that she must not even have been betrothed, so the divorced ארוסה is excluded. 'לאיש' teaches that only being with a man removes her status, so the מוכת עץ is still included.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי reads 'לא היתה לאיש' in two parts. 'לא היתה' excludes the divorced ארוסה. 'לאיש' keeps the מוכת עץ included.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the opposite of the result in steps 1-6. There, the מוכת עץ was excluded and the divorced ארוסה included. רבי יוסי holds the reverse.

phrases.english: One from 'has not been',
phrases.notes: This part teaches she must not even have been betrothed.

phrases.english: and one from 'with a man'.
phrases.notes: This part teaches that only being with a man counts, so a מוכת עץ is still included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the phrase into two separate teachings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לא היתה לאיש' is one unit that can teach only one law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each half of the phrase teaches its own law, so both of רבי יוסי's rulings have a source.

steps.title: Does 'to him' clash with 'complete virgin'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says 'אליו' includes a בוגרת. But he also says 'בתולה' means a complete virgin. Those seem to clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To him' comes to include a grown woman. But didn't רבי שמעון say that 'virgin' means a complete virgin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls רבי שמעון's teaching that 'אליו' includes a בוגרת. It then challenges it with another teaching of his, that 'בתולה' means only a complete virgin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a בוגרת is still treated as a בתולה through 'אליו', it looks odd for רבי שמעון to say elsewhere that 'בתולה' excludes her. The גמרא wants to know how both statements fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To him', a word in the פסוק about the כהן's sister
A grown young woman, past the stage of נערה
A complete virgin, with every sign of virginity

phrases.english: "To him" comes to include a grown woman.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:3, about the sister a כהן may become impure for.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Shimon say:
"Virgin" means a complete virgin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי יוסי's sources to a possible clash between two of רבי שמעון's own teachings.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's reading that 'אליו' includes a בוגרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling a בוגרת a בתולה through 'אליו' seems to contradict his rule that 'בתולה' means only a complete virgin.

steps.title: The two teachings actually come from one source
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's 'complete virgin' rule is itself learned from 'אליו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: His reason there also comes from here. He reasons like this: since 'to him' is needed to include a grown woman, we learn that 'virgin' alone means a complete virgin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two teachings do not clash. One is actually the source of the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word 'בתולה' already included a בוגרת, the תורה would not need 'אליו' to add her. So the extra word itself shows that plain 'בתולה' means a complete virgin. The 'contradiction' turns out to be one argument.

keyTerms.meaning: He expounds, he reads the פסוק this way

steps.whatToRemember: An extra word that is needed to include something shows that the basic word, on its own, does not include it.

phrases.english: His reason there as well
comes from here, because he expounds like this:
since "to him" is needed to include a grown woman,
we infer that "virgin" means a complete virgin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing that one teaching is built on the other.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two statements are shown to come from one source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two teachings of רבי שמעון seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The need for 'אליו' is exactly what proves that plain 'בתולה' means a complete virgin.

steps.title: A convert under three may marry a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי rules that a גיורת who converted before three years and a day may marry a כהן. He proves it from the war with מדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says a female convert younger than three years and one day may marry a כהן. The proof is the פסוק 'all the little ones among the women who have not known a man, keep alive for yourselves', and פנחס was with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא from רבי שמעון בן יוחי, again about who counts as a בתולה. A very young convert is allowed to marry a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah tells the soldiers to keep the young girls alive 'for yourselves', which רבי שמעון בן יוחי reads as permission to marry them. Since פנחס, a כהן, was among those soldiers, these girls must be permitted even to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl of three years and one day, the age from which relations count halachically
פנחס, the כהן who went out with the army against מדין

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:

phrases.aramaic: גִּיּוֹרֶת פְּחוּתָה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: A female convert younger than three years and one day
is permitted to marry into the priesthood,
as it is said:
"And all the little ones among the women
who have not known lying with a male
keep alive for yourselves,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:18, after the war with מדין.

phrases.english: and פנחס was with them.
phrases.notes: פנחס was a כהן and went out with the army (במדבר 31:6), so 'for yourselves' included him too.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic that is related, since it also deals with who counts as a בתולה for כהונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גיורת who converted before three years and one day may marry a כהן.

steps.title: How do the רבנן read the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who disagree, explain 'keep alive for yourselves'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with this פסוק, since they do not accept רבי שמעון בן יוחי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק seems to prove that young converts are permitted to a כהן, the רבנן who argue need some other reading of it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority who disagree here

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing view handles the proof from the previous step.

steps.title: The רבנן: kept as servants, not as wives
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say 'for yourselves' means as servants, not for marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: As male and female servants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן read 'keep alive for yourselves' as keeping the girls to serve, not to marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'for yourselves' means servants, the פסוק says nothing about marrying a כהן. So the proof from פנחס does not work for the רבנן.

phrases.english: As male servants and maidservants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the רבנן's reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'For yourselves' means as servants, so marriage, and a כהן, are not in the picture.

steps.title: Why stop at three years and a day?
steps.stepSummary: If the source is this פסוק, an older girl who has never been with a man should also be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a girl of three years and one day should also be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בן יוחי. The פסוק only speaks of girls 'who have not known a man', so why limit the ruling by age?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's condition is about actual experience, not age. So any girl who never had relations, even older than three, should fit the פסוק. That makes the age cutoff look baseless.

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: בַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד נָמֵי?
phrases.english: a girl of three years and one day as well?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי שמעון בן יוחי's ruling and questions its age limit.
steps.kashyaTarget: The cutoff of three years and one day in רבי שמעון בן יוחי's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's condition is 'not known a man', which an older girl can also meet, so the age limit does not seem to come from the פסוק.

steps.title: The answer follows רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the age limit is explained by רב הונא's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רב הונא's teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא says the answer comes from רב הונא, and then quotes his teaching in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of answering directly, the גמרא points to an existing teaching of רב הונא that explains why age, not just experience, matters in these פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: Following the teaching of רב הונא

phrases.english: As in the teaching of Rav Huna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge about the age limit.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings in an outside teaching that explains the age limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The age limit seems to have no basis in the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא's reading of the פסוקים will show why three years and one day is the line.

steps.title: רב הונא: two פסוקים about the girls seem to clash
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק implies young girls are kept alive no matter what. The next implies girls who had relations must be killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא pointed out a contradiction. One פסוק says, 'Kill every woman who has known a man by lying with a male', so a woman who has not known a man is kept alive, which means the little ones are kept alive whether or not they have known a man. But another פסוק says, 'All the little ones among the women who have not known lying with a male, keep alive for yourselves', so if they have known a man, they are killed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב הונא's contradiction between two neighboring פסוקים about the girls of מדין. This sets up the resolution that will explain the three-years-and-a-day limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק speaks only of 'women', so it seems little girls are spared even if they had relations. The second פסוק spares only the little ones who did not have relations, so it seems those who did are killed. Answering this clash will show what kind of 'knowing' counts for a young girl.

keyTerms.meaning: Pointed out a contradiction between two sources
Has known a man, has had relations

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here. רב הונא answers this contradiction in the next step, and that answer explains the age of three years and one day.

phrases.english: For Rav Huna raised a contradiction:
It is written:
"Every woman who has known a man
by lying with a male, kill,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:17

phrases.english: so one who has not known a man, keep alive,
which implies that the little ones,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין יָדְעוּ בֵּין לֹא יָדְעוּ — קַיֵּימוּ.
phrases.english: whether they have known or have not known a man, keep alive.
And it is written:
"And all the little ones among the women

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָדְעוּ מִשְׁכַּב זָכָר הַחֲיוּ לָכֶם״,
phrases.english: who have not known lying with a male, keep alive for yourselves,"
so if they have known a man, kill them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the רב הונא teaching that the previous step pointed to.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the two פסוקים in במדבר 31 treat little girls who have had relations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פסוק 17 implies little girls are spared even if they had relations, while פסוק 18 implies those who had relations are killed.

steps.title: The verse is talking about a girl old enough for relations
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא resolves the contradiction between the two פסוקים. The Torah is talking about a girl who is fit for relations, meaning old enough, and not about whether she actually had relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: You must say that the פסוק is talking about a girl who is old enough to be fit for relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב הונא's answer to the contradiction raised in Step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא answers that 'knew a man' really means 'old enough to be fit for it,' so the dividing line is age, not what actually happened. This also answers the question of step 16: a girl of three years and one day is already 'fit for relations,' so the פסוק does not spare her, and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's permission stops below that age.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say; this is the only way to read it
Fit for relations, meaning old enough that relations count legally

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'fit for relations' as 'had relations.' The whole point is that the פסוק is about age, not about what actually happened.

phrases.english: You must say
the verse is speaking of one who is fit for relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר בִּרְאוּיָה לִיבָּעֵל הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 18 between the two פסוקים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Knew a man' means a girl who actually had relations, so it clashes with the next פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Knew a man' means a girl old enough to be fit for relations, so the dividing line is age.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב הונא. It proves from the next פסוק that 'every woman that has known a man' must mean one fit for relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: 'And every woman that has known a man' means one fit for relations. You might ask: does it mean one fit for relations, or only one who actually had relations? Since the next פסוק says 'But all the young ones among the women who have not known a man,' you must say it means one fit for relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב הונא. This backs up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא raises the same doubt as Step 18 and settles it the same way. The second פסוק spares only the 'young ones,' so older girls are not spared even if they never had relations. That only makes sense if the first פסוק is about being old enough.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא; a support
When it says; introduces proof from another פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב הונא's reading is not just one אמורא's idea. An earlier ברייתא already read the פסוקים this way.

phrases.english: It is also taught so in a ברייתא:
"And every woman that has known a man"
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:17

phrases.english: the verse is speaking of one fit for relations.
Do you say it means one fit for relations,
or perhaps it means only one who actually had relations?
When it says:
"But all the young ones among the women
who have not known lying with a male,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:18

phrases.english: you must say:
the verse is speaking of one fit for relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports רב הונא's answer in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's reading that the פסוק is about a girl old enough to be fit for relations
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads במדבר 31:17 in light of 31:18

steps.title: How did they know which girls were old enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a practical question: how could the soldiers know which girls were old enough to be fit for relations?
steps.simpleTranslation: How did they know?
steps.whatsHappening: The הלכה is now clear, so the גמרא asks how it was carried out. How could anyone tell a girl's category? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule now depends on age, but there were no records of each captive girl's age. The גמרא wants to know how they could sort the girls correctly.

phrases.english: From where did they know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the meaning of the פסוק to how it was carried out in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How they identified which captive girls were fit for relations

steps.title: The girls were passed before the ציץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון חסידא says the girls were passed in front of the ציץ. The face of any girl who was fit for relations miraculously turned pale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר ביזנא said in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא: They passed the girls in front of the ציץ. Any girl whose face turned pale was known to be fit for relations. Any girl whose face did not turn pale was known not to be fit for relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 21. A miraculous sign from the ציץ showed which girls were old enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No ordinary test could tell their ages, so the answer is a miracle. The ציץ of the כהן גדול made the face of a girl fit for relations turn pale. A girl who was not fit stayed as she was.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden plate worn on the forehead of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Bizna said
that Rabbi Shimon Ḥasida said:
They passed them before the frontplate.
phrases.notes: The ציץ is the golden plate on the כהן גדול's forehead.

phrases.english: Any girl whose face turned pale,
it was known that she was fit for relations;
any girl whose face did not turn pale,
it was known that she was not fit for relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר בִּיזְנָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן חֲסִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the practical question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They passed the girls before the ציץ, and a pale face showed that a girl was fit for relations.

steps.title: A pale-face illness as a sign of sin
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן adds a related statement: the illness הדרוקן, which makes the face pale, is a sign of sexual sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: A sign of sin is the illness הדרוקן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a related teaching. It links a pale face to sexual sin, which matches the sign of the ציץ in Step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 used a pale face as the sign. רב נחמן's statement shows that a pale face is a known sign connected to sexual sin, so the ציץ's sign fits a familiar pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: An illness that makes the face pale and swollen

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
A sign of transgression is hidrokan.
phrases.notes: הדרוקן is an illness that makes the face look pale, just like the sign in the last step.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן סִימָן לַעֲבֵירָה הִדְרוֹקָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the idea in Step 22 that a pale face points to sexual matters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The illness הדרוקן, which makes the face pale, is a sign of sexual sin.

steps.title: The same question about the girls of יבש גלעד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a similar case from שופטים. They found 400 young girls in יבש גלעד who had never been with a man, and the גמרא asks how they knew.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a similar way, you can say about the פסוק 'And they found among the people of יבש גלעד four hundred young girls, virgins, who had not known a man': how did they know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel case and asks the same 'how did they know' question about it. This sets up רב כהנא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the question is different from the girls of מדין. It is not about age but about whether the girls really had never been with a man. The פסוק says it plainly, so the גמרא asks how this was checked.

keyTerms.meaning: In a similar way; a parallel case
A city whose people were punished in the story at the end of שופטים
A girl who has never been with a man

phrases.english: Similarly, you can say:
"And they found among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead
four hundred young virgins

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָדְעוּ אִישׁ לְמִשְׁכַּב זָכָר״,
phrases.english: who had not known a man by lying with a male,"
phrases.notes: שופטים 21:12

phrases.english: from where did they know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of practical question from Step 21 to a parallel story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How they knew that the 400 girls of יבש גלעד had never been with a man

steps.title: The wine barrel test
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says they seated the girls on the opening of a barrel of wine. A girl who had been with a man would smell of wine, and a virgin would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: They seated them on the opening of a barrel of wine. If she had been with a man, her breath smelled of wine. If she was a virgin, her breath did not smell of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about יבש גלעד with רב כהנא's test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מדין case, the sign was a miracle from the ציץ. Here the answer is a physical test: the smell of the wine reached only a girl who had been with a man. Both answers explain how a fact stated in a פסוק could actually be known.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has had relations
Her smell spreads; her breath smells of it

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוקים about מדין are about age ('fit for relations'), as רב הונא and a ברייתא teach. The גמרא then explains how they knew: in מדין, through a miracle of the ציץ, and in יבש גלעד, through the wine barrel test.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹשִׁיבוּם עַל פִּי חָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן,
phrases.english: They sat them on the opening of a barrel of wine;
a non-virgin, her breath smelled,
a virgin, her breath did not smell.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא הוֹשִׁיבוּם עַל פִּי חָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They seated the girls on a wine barrel, and only a girl who had been with a man smelled of wine.

steps.title: Why not use the ציץ at יבש גלעד too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the girls of יבש גלעד were not passed in front of the ציץ, the way the girls of מדין were.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why didn't they pass them in front of the ציץ?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב כהנא's barrel-of-wine answer. At מדין they used the ציץ, so why not use it here too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 showed that the ציץ could miraculously reveal which girls were fit for relations. If that method was available, the wine barrel seems unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know why the ציץ was not used for the girls of יבש גלעד.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden plate worn on the forehead of the כהן גדול
Let them pass them (in front of something)

phrases.english: Let them pass them before the frontplate!
phrases.notes: He means: do it the way they did with the girls of מדין back in step 22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the barrel method from step 25 by pointing to the ציץ method from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's explanation that the barrel of wine was used at יבש גלעד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A miraculous method (the ציץ) already worked at מדין, so why was a different method needed?

steps.title: The ציץ is only for acceptance, not for punishment
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא בריה דרב נתן answers from the פסוק "לרצון להם": the ציץ brings acceptance, not punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא son of רב נתן said: It is written "for acceptance for them." That means acceptance, not punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא בריה דרב נתן explains why the ציץ could not be used for Jewish girls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the ציץ is "לרצון", meaning it brings favor and acceptance. Using it to expose Jewish girls would turn it into a tool of punishment, which the פסוק rules out.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana, son of Rav Natan, said:
"For acceptance for them" is written,
phrases.notes: שמות 28:38

phrases.english: for acceptance, and not for calamity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ציץ's function based on a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ציץ could be used anywhere to reveal hidden facts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ציץ may only be used for acceptance, never to bring disgrace or punishment.

steps.title: Then why was the ציץ used at מדין?
steps.stepSummary: If the ציץ is never for punishment, it should not have been used at מדין either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then at מדין too, it should not have been used!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer back against the story of מדין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said the ציץ was used on the girls of מדין. That also exposed them, which looks like a kind of punishment. So the rule "not for calamity" seems to clash with the מדין story.

keyTerms.meaning: The nation of מדין, whose girls were checked with the ציץ

phrases.english: If so, in Midian also?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 27 using the account in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא בריה דרב נתן's rule that the ציץ is not for calamity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ציץ was in fact used at מדין to single out girls for death, which seems to contradict the rule.

steps.title: The rule applies only to the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads the word "להם" closely: for the Jewish people the ציץ is only for acceptance, but for non-Jews it can also bring punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is written "for them." For them, the Jewish people, it is for acceptance and not for punishment. For non-Jews, it can be even for punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי resolves the difficulty by limiting the rule to Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word "להם" narrows the rule to the Jewish people. The girls of מדין were not Jewish, so using the ציץ on them was allowed. The girls of יבש גלעד were Jewish, so a different method, the wine barrel, was needed.
steps.whatToRemember: The ציץ only brings favor to the Jewish people. With non-Jews it could also expose and punish, which is why it was used at מדין but not at יבש גלעד.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
"For them" is written,
for them, for acceptance and not for calamity;
but for gentiles, even for calamity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 by narrowing the rule from step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule to a specific group using an extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ציץ can never be used for punishment, so the מדין story is a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule protects only Jews. For non-Jews like the girls of מדין, the ציץ may be used even for calamity.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי reports in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אידי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main legal question and gives a ruling on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי holds that a convert girl younger than three years and a day may marry a כהן. This step gives a final ruling in his favor, in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns the earlier disagreement into a practical ruling, and the rest of the section checks how reliable that ruling is.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai.
phrases.notes: This goes back to his view earlier on the daf, that a convert girl under three years and a day may marry a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the ציץ and returns to the main מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.

steps.title: Did you hear it directly or only infer it?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבי יעקב בר אידי whether he heard this ruling clearly from רבי יהושע בן לוי or only figured it out from something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי יעקב בר אידי: Did you hear it explicitly, or did you hear it by inference?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא questions where the ruling came from. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling that was said outright carries more weight than one figured out from a story. רבי זירא wants to know which kind of ruling this was.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, worked out from something else

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi:
Did you hear it explicitly,
or did you hear it by inference?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפֵירוּשׁ שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ, אוֹ מִכְּלָלָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source of the ruling in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהושע בן לוי stated the ruling outright or whether it was inferred.

steps.title: What inference did רבי זירא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which inference רבי זירא had in mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: What inference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask what רבי זירא was hinting at. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא spoke of an "inference" but did not say what it was. The גמרא wants to identify the case from which רבי יהושע בן לוי's view could have been worked out.

phrases.english: What inference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the word מכללא in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which teaching could have been the basis for inferring the ruling.

steps.title: The story of רבי רומנוס and the convert girl
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי told of a family whose lineage was questioned. רבי sent רבי רומנוס to check, and רבי approved a convert girl under three years and a day for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יהושע בן לוי said: There was a city in ארץ ישראל whose lineage was challenged. רבי sent רבי רומנוס, and he checked it. He found in it a convert girl younger than three years and a day, and רבי declared her fit for כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the story that could be the source of the inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because רבי יהושע בן לוי told this story, in which רבי allowed a young convert girl to a כהן, one might conclude that he holds like רבי שמעון בן יוחאי. That would be a ruling learned only by inference.

keyTerms.meaning: A challenge to a family's lineage
Declared her fit to be married to a כהן

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
There was one city in Eretz Yisrael
about which a challenge was raised,

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁגֵּר רַבִּי אֶת רַבִּי רוֹמָנוּס וּבְדָקָהּ,
phrases.english: and Rabbi sent Rabbi Romanus, and he examined it,
phrases.notes: "רבי" alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and he found in it a girl who was a convert

phrases.aramaic: פְּחוּתָה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: younger than three years and one day,
and Rabbi declared her fit for the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: עִיר אַחַת הָיְתָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 32 by naming the story behind the possible inference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The inference would come from רבי יהושע בן לוי's story in which רבי approved a young convert girl for כהונה.

steps.title: I heard it directly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי answers that he heard the ruling explicitly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I heard it explicitly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב בר אידי answers רבי זירא's question from step 31.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling did not come from the story. רבי יהושע בן לוי said it outright, so it stands on firm ground.

phrases.english: He said to him: I heard it explicitly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to the question in step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling was stated explicitly, not inferred.

steps.title: What would be wrong with an inference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the difference would be if the ruling had come only from the story.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it was by inference, what of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי זירא cared about this. It is setting up an explanation of why the story is weak proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story seems to show clearly that רבי permitted the girl. So the גמרא asks what problem there would be in relying on it.

phrases.english: And if by inference, what of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the difference raised in step 31 matters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a ruling learned from the story would be less reliable.

steps.title: The story may be about a marriage that already happened
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the girl was allowed only because she was already married. A comparison is brought from רב and רבי יוחנן, who say a בוגרת or מוכת עץ should not be married, but if she was, the marriage stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is different there: since she was already married, she stays married. As רב and רבי יוחנן both say: He should not marry a בוגרת or a מוכת עץ, but if he married her, he stays married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the story would be weak proof. רבי may only have let an existing marriage stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Allowing a marriage to stand after it already happened is not the same as allowing it from the start. רב and רבי יוחנן show such a case: a woman who may not be married at first, yet the marriage is not undone. So the story does not prove רבי יהושע בן לוי holds like רבי שמעון בן יוחאי from the start, which is why it mattered that the ruling was heard directly.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman whose hymen was torn by accident

steps.whatToRemember: This is only a suggestion for why the story might not prove the ruling. The next step rejects it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as rejecting the ruling. The ruling stands because it was heard directly. This step only shows why the story alone would not have been enough proof.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different there:
since she was married, she stays married.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא רַב וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: For Rav and Rabbi Yoḥanan both say:
He may not marry a grown woman or one whose hymen was torn by accident,
phrases.notes: This is about a כהן גדול, who must marry a בתולה.

phrases.english: but if he married her, he is married.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם: הוֹאִיל וְאִנְּסִיב — אִנְּסִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 35 by showing the weakness of the inference from step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The story may only show that an existing marriage is allowed to stand, not that such a marriage is allowed from the start.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the story, not the ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story is about a marriage that had already taken place, which may be more lenient than permitting one from the start.

steps.title: The comparison to a grown woman does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison from step 36. A בוגרת or מוכת עץ will end up that way under her husband anyway, so allowing her after the fact makes sense. But a convert will never turn into a זונה under him, so if she were truly forbidden, she would be forbidden even after marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them?! There, it makes sense: she would eventually become a grown woman while married to him, and she would eventually stop being a virgin while married to him. But here, will she eventually become a זונה while married to him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea from step 36 that רבי only allowed the convert girl because she was already married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בוגרת or מוכת עץ is only a problem at the start. Married life would bring her to that same state anyway, so an existing marriage can stand. A convert who is forbidden is forbidden because she counts as a זונה, and marriage never turns a woman into a זונה. So her marriage would not stand after the fact either, which means the story really does prove that רבי ruled like רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (a phrase that rejects a comparison)
Under him, meaning while married to him
A woman who is not a virgin
A woman forbidden to a כהן, here because of her status as a convert

steps.whatToRemember: Allowing a woman after the fact only works when married life would bring her to that state anyway. A זונה problem is never solved by marriage, so the story with רבי really does show that רבי (and רבי יהושע בן לוי, who told it) ruled like רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?!
Granted, there:
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of the בוגרת and מוכת עץ from step 36.

phrases.english: she will eventually be a grown woman under him,
she will eventually be a non-virgin under him.
Here, will she eventually be a zona under him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison offered in step 36
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the story with רבי shows only an after-the-fact allowance
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The בוגרת case works only because her husband would bring her to that state anyway. A convert never becomes a זונה through marriage.

steps.title: רב ספרא learned the ruling by inference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב ספרא taught רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling as something inferred from the story, not as something said outright. He raised the same difficulty and answered it the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא taught this ruling as an inference, and he found it difficult, and he answered it in this same way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a note about how this ruling was passed down: רב ספרא knew it only from the story, not from an explicit statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי יעקב בר אידי in step 34, who heard the ruling outright, רב ספרא worked it out from the story. Because of that, he faced the same question of steps 35 and 36, that maybe it was only after the fact. He answered it the way step 37 did.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, worked out rather than heard directly

phrases.english: Rav Safra taught it by inference
and it was difficult for him,
phrases.notes: "It" is the question from step 36: maybe רבי allowed her only because she was already married.

phrases.english: and he answered (it) this way.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't; the meaning is the same either way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains who actually needed the reasoning of steps 35 through 37
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ספרא knew רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling only by inference from the story, and he settled the difficulty the same way the גמרא did.

steps.title: A כהן marries a young convert based on רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: A כהן married a convert who converted before age three years and a day. When רב נחמן בר יצחק asked him what he was doing, he quoted רבי יעקב בר אידי in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain כהן married a convert who was younger than three years and one day. רב נחמן בר יצחק said to him: What is this? He answered: Because רבי יעקב בר אידי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case where someone acted on this ruling. It is setting up רב נחמן בר יצחק's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן was relying on exactly the ruling stated in step 30 and confirmed as heard directly in step 34. רב נחמן בר יצחק's question "What is this?" shows that he saw the marriage as a problem. The story is built so that his strong reaction comes next.

keyTerms.term: פְּחוּתָה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
keyTerms.meaning: Younger than three years and one day
What is this? (a challenge to someone's behavior)

phrases.english: A certain priest who married a convert

phrases.aramaic: פְּחוּתָה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: less than three years and one day old.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַאי הַאי?
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said to him: What is this?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי
phrases.english: He said to him: As Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ruling from step 30 being used in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן relied on the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחאי and married a convert who converted before age three years and a day.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק orders the כהן to divorce her
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the כהן's reliance on רבי יעקב בר אידי. He orders him to divorce her, and warns that otherwise he will force him to stop following that opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go, send her away. And if not, I will pull רבי יעקב בר אידי out of your ear!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק firmly refuses to accept the כהן's source and tells him to divorce his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the ruling came with a solid chain of names, רב נחמן בר יצחק would not let anyone act on it. He tells the כהן to end the marriage. The colorful phrase means: I will make you stop following what you heard from רבי יעקב בר אידי.

keyTerms.meaning: Go, send her out, meaning divorce her

steps.confusionAlert: "I will take רבי יעקב בר אידי out of your ear" is not a threat to hurt anyone. It means: I will make you stop following the ruling you heard from him.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go remove her,
phrases.notes: "Remove" here means divorce her.

phrases.english: and if not, I will remove for you
Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi from your ear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the כהן's justification in step 39
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Relying on רבי יעקב בר אידי's report to allow this marriage in practice
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב נחמן בר יצחק does not accept this ruling as something to act on, so the marriage must end.

steps.title: Introducing a ברייתא with רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a ברייתא that quotes another teaching of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי. The teaching itself begins on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: And so too רבי שמעון בן יוחאי would say:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote a ברייתא with more of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's words, and the actual teaching comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "and so too" link the coming teaching to the earlier quotes from רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, as another of his statements. Nothing is ruled yet. This line only opens the source, and its content comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too he would say

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: And similarly, Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai would say:

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having finished with רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's ruling about a young convert, the גמרא opens another teaching of his.
steps.raayaObject: The view of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחאי (its content follows in the next line)
